reading_text: The birch stands out early in green, its small leaves open while the ground beneath it holds the last of the cold. Then all of it falls away but that one tree, leafing before it has any proof of warmth. This is Berkana, the growth that starts before the season agrees to it. Are you moving with the ground you stand on, or ahead of it?

The fog sits heavy on the fjord and swallows the far shore whole. The Blank is that grey where the water gives back nothing yet, Anna, and shows no line to steer by. You stand at the edge of it, and the fog does not lift on command.

Where the doorway ends and the room begins, Anna, the coffee waits and the second cup steams beside your own. Gebo is that unhurried welcome, the way a threshold widens when it is shared. Some warmth only grows once there is someone to pour for.

You come up the dark road and see the one lamp burning in the window, kept lit for your return. Algiz is that keeping-watch, the light that holds while you decide which way home. Both roads pass under it, and it does not go out.

The egg lies whole in the nest, warm and unmarked, and nothing of what it holds shows yet. This is Ingwaz, the slow gathering of a thing not ready to be seen. Whichever way you stand, the shell stays quiet a while longer.

The voice on the phone says the words, Anna, and in the saying they cross from air into something you can hold. Ansuz is that turning, where a sound becomes a thing that stays. You stand now at the door with the receiver still warm in your hand.

The coffee sits cooling, its steam long gone, while the seat across from you stays empty and the waiting holds you in place. Isa is that stillness where nothing crosses the distance between two people. The cup goes cold, and the table keeps its silence.

Two horses climb the mountain together, matching stride for stride, neither pulling ahead nor falling behind. This is Ehwaz, the trust that lets two move as one without a rope between them. The pace is not one animal's doing, but something found in the space between their steps. It holds only as long as both keep watching the ground the other walks.

At the edge where dough turns to bread, the crust hardens while the middle stays soft and warm. Fehu is that warmth broken and passed across the table, one hand to another. What is shared does not shrink in the giving, it feeds more than the one who made it. You stand with the loaf between you, still steaming, not yet cut.

You step in from the cold, and the doorway gives way to a room where someone has already lit the stove. Wunjo is that warmth waiting before you knew you needed it, kindled by another hand. The chill leaves your fingers slowly, at the pace the room allows. You stand just inside, in the first heat, your coat still on.

Below the bright hayfield, in the soil no light reaches, the roots hold what the day cannot see. This is Sowilo, the long sun that keeps things growing past the hour they should rest. What passes between two people carries on the same way, warm long after the words have stopped. You stand in that late brightness, Anna, where the field never quite goes dark.

Behind the door those keys once opened, other hands now move through the rooms. This is Othila, the loosening of a grip on what was yours to keep. The metal cools in your palm, no lock left in your life to fit it. You stand at the gate with the keys still warm, the road past it unwalked.

The next cairn stands beyond the rise, not yet in view, waiting for you to reach the stone in front of you first. Raidho is that walking from marker to marker, each one shown only by the last. You stand at the cairn you can see.

The bowl stays covered while the dough beneath it swells at its own pace. Jera is the slow work that answers to time, not to your hand on the lid. You may have already chosen the hour to begin, sure the rising has finished, and still the warmth decides. You are standing at the counter, waiting on something that will not be pressed.

See the single reed at the lagoon's edge, its reflection breaking at the least breath of air. Mannaz is your own face on that water, clear one moment and rippling the next as you look at what you make. The stillness returns on its own, Anna.

Where the lava field cooled, its edge still holds the fire that shaped it, though the moss has crept in green and quiet over the black stone. Uruz is that old heat working under what looks finished, the ground remaking itself without asking. What set you moving is still in the rock beneath your feet. You stand at the seam where hard stone turns soft with moss.
